data.exact_reserve_text: In 2016, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 20.1m (2015: GBP 27.1m) due primarily to a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts following lower than expected incurred claims movements during 2016 and a release of catastrophe loads on 2015 year of account as policies come off risk.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a gross prior year reserve release of GBP 20.1 million in 2016. This release was primarily driven by a reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims from 2013 and prior accounts, as well as a release of catastrophe loads from the 2015 year of account as policies came off risk. There was also a slight reduction in the ultimate gross loss for Superstorm Sandy, contributing to the release, although international catastrophe events from 2010/11 saw a further provision.
raw_causal_phrases: reduction in the assessment of medical malpractice claims on the 2013 and prior accounts
lower than expected incurred claims movements during 2016
release of catastrophe loads on 2015 year of account as policies come off risk
The long-tail casualty classes account for around 47% of the back-year release
Older years seem to be settling down relatively smoothly
expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account is GBP 88.5m (GBP 90.3m last year)
further provision of GBP 3.6m (GBP 9.1m last year)
data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development figure of -20.1m is explicitly stated as a gross surplus in ultimate claims in the narrative. The claims triangle calculation yields a different gross PYD (-13.556m), suggesting the narrative figure might include other adjustments not visible in the triangle or a different scope. The narrative figure is prioritized due to its explicit statement.
